summary: Compose the qualified Bitrix24 CRM adapter through the host-owned OAuth and HTTPS runtime on a dedicated CRM surface.

impacts.evidence: CRM account configuration and SecretProvider callbacks remain organization/workspace scoped through the existing connector-account boundary.
CRM records are not copied into new persistence; token material remains excluded from normal records, logs, events and API views.
Existing account, OAuth, runtime-config, capability and health operations are reused without public schema changes.
No event names or payloads change.
The existing SDK CRM reader/writer contracts are composed unchanged behind the built-in registry.
Existing connector-account and runtime-config tables support the admitted CRM surface; no migration or backfill is required.
Portal host validation and common DNS-pinned public HTTPS egress are enforced; only current OAuth access tokens reach the adapter.
CRM write capabilities remain explicitly disabled by default and are independently selected on the account; generic product sync is not enabled.
Existing account credential/configuration/capability and health audit events cover the new composition without secret-bearing payloads.
Bitrix24 adapter read-before/write and ambiguous-outcome reconciliation remain the only success path for CRM writes.
Only portal REST egress through the common transport is added; inbound Bitrix24 events remain deferred.
Existing bounded connector health states and normalized remote error categories apply to the CRM account.
Rollback removes CRM admission from new requests without deleting existing account/configuration data or remote records.
Registry admission, support contract generation, transport composition, frontend and existing Bitrix24 conformance tests cover the change.
